fluff.overview:
The Thug was introduced in 2572 by the Maltex Corporation as a direct competitor to the popular Warhammer. Designed for the Star League Defense Force, the eighty-ton assault 'Mech sought to address the Warhammer's key weaknesses, particularly its thin armor protection, while retaining comparable firepower. The result was one of the hardiest BattleMechs ever produced, earning a reputation as the quintessential "zombie 'Mech" for its ability to absorb punishment and keep fighting.

Demand quickly outstripped Maltex's production capacity on Errai, forcing the company to license production to Earthwerks Incorporated on Keystone. The destruction of Maltex's facilities in 2835 left Earthwerks as the sole manufacturer for centuries, producing a downgraded variant until technological recovery allowed both companies to resume original-specification production during the 3050s. Despite never fully replacing the Warhammer, the Thug has remained a mainstay of Inner Sphere heavy assault formations for over five hundred years.
fluff.capabilities:
The Thug's design philosophy prioritizes durability and sustained firepower. Its primary armament consists of two arm-mounted Tiegart Particle Projection Cannons, similar in performance to those found on the Warhammer but ten percent smaller with additional redundancies built in. Backing up the PPCs are a pair of Bical SRM-6 launchers, each fed from its own CASE-protected ammunition bin, providing devastating close-range firepower against exposed internals or enemies that close the distance. Each SRM tube features a dilating protective cover when not in use.

What truly sets the Thug apart from its rivals is its exceptional survivability. The Earthwerks VOL endo steel chassis saves enough weight to mount fifteen and a half tons of Mitchell Argon armor, over fifty percent more protection than the Warhammer carries. Eighteen double heat sinks provide far superior heat management, allowing sustained PPC fire without the crippling heat buildup that plagues many energy-heavy designs. The Thug also benefits from fully functional hand actuators, making it a surprisingly capable close-quarters combatant and an effective raider.

The primary trade-off is the Thug's modest cruising speed of forty-three kilometers per hour, leaving the design reliant on support elements for flank protection.
fluff.history:
The Thug's history begins in the last decades before the Reunification War, when the newly formed Star League sought the most capable military hardware available. In 2572, the Maltex Corporation unveiled the THG-11E as a direct answer to the Warhammer, promising superior protection and comparable firepower. The design proved an immediate success with the SLDF, and demand grew rapidly enough that Maltex was forced to license Earthwerks Incorporated to establish a second production line on Keystone. A third line operated at Earthwerks' Tikonov facility under Capellan Confederation oversight. Throughout the Star League period, the Thug served with distinction in garrison and assault formations across the Inner Sphere, with the THG-11Eb Royal variant entering service with elite SLDF brigades in 2760.

The fall of the Star League and the onset of the Succession Wars proved catastrophic for Thug production. Maltex Corporation's Errai factory was destroyed in 2835, eliminating the primary production source, while the Tikonov facility had already ceased operations. Only Earthwerks' Keystone line remained active. The loss of advanced technology forced Earthwerks to develop the downgraded THG-10E variant. In an ironic twist, it was the Warhammer that kept the Thug alive. With original Tiegart PPCs unavailable, Earthwerks reworked the design to utilize the extensive stockpile of Donal PPCs from Warhammer production, enabling continued manufacture and easier field repairs. The 10E also substituted standard construction for endo steel, single heat sinks for doubles, and Holly SRM-4 launchers for the original Bical SRM-6s.

Despite these compromises, the Thug remained a valued asset throughout the Succession Wars. Even in its downgraded form, it offered superior armor protection compared to most contemporaries and its hand actuators remained a prized feature for raiding operations. The largest concentration of original THG-11E models during this period belonged to ComStar, whose secret Com Guards maintained Star League-era equipment in pristine condition. Elements of Hansen's Roughriders famously raided Delacruz in 3038, where a pair of Thugs held off an entire company of defenders while the rest of the unit emptied a supply warehouse of spare parts and ammunition before successfully retreating off-world.

The technological renaissance of the 3040s and 3050s breathed new life into the Thug program. Recovery of lostech enabled both Earthwerks and the rebuilt Maltex Corporation to resume production of original-specification THG-11E models. The formation of the Second Star League spurred development of several new variants. The THG-12E, built for ComStar and the Word of Blake in 3067, upgraded the PPCs to extended-range models and integrated a C3i battle computer. Maltex also produced the THG-12K for the Draconis Combine, substituting a standard C3 slave unit and Guardian ECM suite. The most radical departure was the THG-13K, which abandoned the proven missile armament entirely in favor of three heavy PPCs and an extra-light engine, a configuration that traded the Thug's legendary survivability for devastating alpha-strike capability.

The Jihad era saw the Thug pressed into service by all major powers. The Word of Blake seized Maltex's Errai facility during the conflict, while Earthwerks' Keystone line served forces aligned with the Free Worlds League. Production was split among ComStar, the reforming SLDF, the DCMS, and the AFFS. The post-Jihad period brought further changes as the Republic of the Sphere absorbed former Word of Blake territories including Errai.

The Dark Age saw the Thug's production theater shift once more. Maltex's Errai facility, eventually falling under Draconis Combine control, resumed production of the THG-12K and introduced the THG-13U, a modern brawler variant mounting twin snub-nose PPCs, quad MML-3 launchers, triple-strength myomer, and a supercharger, all protected by twenty tons of ballistic-reinforced armor. The Thug's continued evolution five centuries after its introduction stands as proof of the fundamental soundness of Maltex's original vision, a heavily armored, hard-hitting assault 'Mech capable of standing toe-to-toe with anything on the battlefield.
fluff.deployment: This experimental custom refit was produced at Maltex Corporation's Errai facility in late 2772 for a mercenary operating with Amaris forces during the fall of the Star League. The design replaces the standard engine with an extralight model and removes the PPCs in favor of two extended-range large lasers. The weight savings allowed installation of three additional SRM-6 launchers for a total of five, along with four jump jets and a null-signature system that interfered with SLDF targeting sensors. A command console permits a second officer to coordinate tactical operations from the cockpit. The design was rendered obsolete by 2776.
